title: lazyrunner project profile
description: What a project is for lazyrunner: the file that marks its repo, the folder whose changes need a rebuild, and the apps it runs. Schema version 1 (projects/README.md). In a repo's .lazyrunner.json, detect can be left out, and with extends only the changes are needed.

$schema.description: Lets editors check the file; lazyrunner ignores it.

schemaVersion.description: The profile format version. lazyrunner refuses a version it doesn't know.

extends.description: Only in a repo's .lazyrunner.json: the id of a known profile this file changes. Its top-level fields replace that profile's; apps merge by key.

id.description: Short lowercase name. Names the project's settings in lazyrunner.config.json and its state folder.

detect.description: How lazyrunner recognises the repo. Required, except in a repo's .lazyrunner.json (that file marks the repo).

anyFile.description: A file only this project's repo has, relative to its root. lazyrunner looks for it upward from the current folder. One file for now.

watch.description: The folder whose changes need a rebuild of the .NET apps (unchanged builds are skipped; restart on code change). One folder for now.

apps.description: The apps lazyrunner runs, left to right as its columns: .NET apps, npm apps and command apps (the tables below).

tasks.description: Optional. One-off commands run from the palette or by an agent (the task table below).

presets.description: Optional. This profile's own presets, by name: a command app's "preset" finds them before yours and lazyrunner's (the preset table below).

layers.description: Optional. Rules for the code map (K, then Tab): each key a project's name (* for anything, e.g. *.Api), and the projects it must not reference - a link that does is marked as a rule break. Nx's module boundaries (.eslintrc.json's depConstraints) are read as well.

mustNotReference.description: Project names (or patterns) it must not reference.

health.title: An app's health ("health")
health.description: Optional, on a .NET, npm or command app. What the Stack screen's Health tab (K) holds the app to, and what its response-time probe asks for. A reading over its target for a minute is an alert - the log says so, the app's title flashes and a notification goes out - until it recovers; a on the Health tab acknowledges it. Without it: p95 1000 ms, 5% 5xx, 2048 MB, 90% CPU.

p95Ms.description: Optional. The p95 latency over the last minute, in milliseconds (a .NET app whose requests are logged). Default 1000.

errorRate.description: Optional. The share of 5xx answers over the last minute, judged from 10 requests on (a .NET app whose requests are logged). Default 0.05.

memoryMb.description: Optional. Memory of the app's whole process tree, in MB. Default 2048.

cpuPercent.description: Optional. CPU of the app's whole process tree, as a percent of the machine. Default 90.

path.description: Optional. The app's own health endpoint: the response-time probe asks for it instead of the Swagger page (or /).

expectedStatus.description: Optional. The status the probe expects; any other counts as not responding. Without it any answer counts.

relativePath.description: Relative to the repo root; / or \ both work.

appKey.description: Lowercase letters and digits, starting with a letter.

icon.description: One character before the app's name in its title bar.

nerdIcon.description: Optional. Its icon in the title bar when Nerd Font icons are on (nerdIcons): one Nerd Font character. Without it .NET's, or the framework's in package.json (Angular, React, Vue) else Node.js's, as a JSON escape (\uf0ac, a globe) or the character itself.

dotnetApp.title: A .NET app ("type": "dotnet")
dotnetApp.description: An ASP.NET (or any dotnet run) project. lazyrunner builds it with dotnet build, one build at a time and skipped when nothing in watch changed, then runs it with dotnet run --no-build --launch-profile.

key.description: Short name, unique in the profile. Used in settings (columnWidths, apps.<key>) and by servedBy.

type.description: The app type: what lazyrunner does with the app follows from it.

launchProfile.description: A profile in the project's Properties/launchSettings.json. Its applicationUrl gives the port.

swagger.description: Optional. The Swagger UI path: lazyrunner probes <swagger>/index.html for the response time, and w opens it. Without it lazyrunner probes /.

args.description: Optional. What dotnet run passes the app besides lazyrunner's own, after --: configuration for local runs, say. An app that logs through Serilog to Seq only prints nothing for the requests view (H); an empty Seq key (--Seq:ApiKey=) brings its console log back, when its code reads it that way.

env.description: Optional. Environment variables the app gets on top of lazyrunner's own (x then e shows them).

tests.description: Optional. Test suites that belong to this app in the tests view (T), whatever lazyrunner works out: .NET test projects by path from the repo root or by name, Nx projects by name. Without it a .NET test project belongs to the app whose project it references, an npm or Nx suite to the npm app whose folder it runs in.

dependsOn.description: Optional. The apps it calls, by key: the stack map (K) draws these edges dashed until a call is seen (a .NET app's own calls are seen in its log without this).

restart.description: Optional. onCrash: when it crashes (exits by itself, not with 0) lazyrunner starts it again after a wait that doubles each time - 1 s, 2 s, 4 s, at most 30 s, starting over once it has stayed up a minute - and holds it after 3 crashes within 2 minutes (u starts it again). A stop you asked for, a restart or a branch change never counts. never (the default): it stays down.

migrations.description: Optional. Where its EF Core migrations are, for the migrations view (M), when lazyrunner shouldn't find them itself (the model snapshots in the app's project and the projects it builds). dotnet ef runs with this app's project as the startup project (its Development settings, the database picked with d) and its last build.

project.description: The project with the migrations, when it isn't the app's own.

contexts.description: Its DbContexts. Without them, those of the model snapshots in project, else what dotnet ef dbcontext list finds.

npmApp.title: An npm app ("type": "npm")
npmApp.description: A folder with package.json, run with npm run <script>. It needs no build from lazyrunner; i runs npm ci for it.

key.description: Short name, unique in the profile.

type.description: The app type: what lazyrunner does with the app follows from it.

variants.description: How it runs, chosen again on every start: the first variant whose when.packageScript package.json has. One without when always applies, so only the last can leave it out.

env.description: Optional. Environment variables the app gets on top of lazyrunner's own (x then e shows them).

tests.description: Optional. Test suites that belong to this app in the tests view (T), whatever lazyrunner works out: .NET test projects by path from the repo root or by name, Nx projects by name. Without it a .NET test project belongs to the app whose project it references, an npm or Nx suite to the npm app whose folder it runs in.

dependsOn.description: Optional. The apps it calls, by key: the stack map (K) draws these edges dashed until a call is seen (a .NET app's own calls are seen in its log without this).

restart.description: Optional. onCrash: when it crashes (exits by itself, not with 0) lazyrunner starts it again after a wait that doubles each time - 1 s, 2 s, 4 s, at most 30 s, starting over once it has stayed up a minute - and holds it after 3 crashes within 2 minutes (u starts it again). A stop you asked for, a restart or a branch change never counts. never (the default): it stays down.

command.description: A command: text split into arguments at spaces (a "quoted part" stays one), or a list of arguments - no shell. Its program is found on PATH, or by its path from cwd (with Windows' extensions); a .ps1 runs in PowerShell. {port} in it is the app's port.

commandApp.title: A command app ("type": "command")
commandApp.description: Any long-running command - a Python, Go or Rust service, a queue emulator, a script - with what .NET and npm apps get, each optional: a build before it starts, an install (i), when it counts as up, what counts as its code (restart on code change), and what its errors and stack frames look like. Stopping takes its whole process tree down.

key.description: Short name, unique in the profile.

type.description: The app type: what lazyrunner does with the app follows from it.

run.description: The long-running command; required unless its preset knows it for this folder.

preset.description: Optional. A preset that fills in each field this app leaves out - by what's in its folder: python (its install by uv.lock or requirements.txt, its .venv on PATH, its errors and stack frames, *.py as its code), go (go mod download, go build, go run . by a main.go) or rust (cargo build, cargo run by a src/main.rs).

path.description: Optional. Folders from cwd (or from your home folder, starting ~/) put first on PATH when they exist, and where its programs are looked for first (a .venv's Scripts, ~/.cargo/bin).

tools.description: Optional. Programs the startup checklist shows with their versions.

cwd.description: Optional. Where it runs, from the repo root (the root without it).

port.description: Optional. Its port: {port} in run, build, install and env is replaced with it, and the ports view (P) and port conflicts see it. Without ready it is up once the port listens.

build.description: Optional. Runs before it starts and on b, one build at a time; skipped when nothing in cwd changed since its last good build (as git sees the folder).

install.description: Optional. Installs its packages, as npm ci does an npm app's: i runs it.

setup.description: Optional. Runs before i's install while none of its own path folders is there - it makes them ([] for none).

installFrom.description: Optional. The files its install installs from, from cwd: when they change since lazyrunner's last install, the startup checklist and the panel say it's due.

ready.description: Optional. When it counts as up: one of port, line or http. Without it, once its port listens - or once it has started, when it has no port.

line.description: Up once a line of its output matches this regular expression.

orPort.description: With line: up once the line shows or its port listens, whichever comes first.

http.description: Up once this path on its port answers with a 2xx (it needs port).

watch.description: Optional. Globs of its code, from cwd (** any folders, * and ? within a name): with restart on code change, saving one restarts it - built first when it builds. .git, .venv, venv, node_modules, target, __pycache__, bin, obj, dist and build are never watched.

errors.description: Optional. Regular expressions of an error line: shown red and counted as an error (the title flashes).

warnings.description: Optional. Regular expressions of a warning line: shown yellow and counted as a warning.

frames.description: Optional. A regular expression of a stack frame with (?P<file>...) and (?P<line>...) groups, and (?P<col>...) when it says: the file becomes a link that opens the editor at its line.

env.description: Optional. Environment variables the app gets on top of lazyrunner's own (x then e shows them); {port} in a value is its port, {cwd} its folder.

dependsOn.description: Optional. The apps it calls, by key: the stack map (K) draws these edges dashed.

restart.description: Optional. onCrash: when it crashes (exits by itself, not with 0) lazyrunner starts it again after a wait that doubles each time - 1 s, 2 s, 4 s, at most 30 s, starting over once it has stayed up a minute - and holds it after 3 crashes within 2 minutes (u starts it again). A stop you asked for, a restart or a branch change never counts. never (the default): it stays down.

composeApp.title: A compose app ("type": "compose")
composeApp.description: Docker Compose services as one app: starting it runs docker compose up for them, its column shows their output and its title each one's state (● up, ◌ starting, ✗ down, ✓ done), and it is up once each runs - healthy, when it has a healthcheck. Stopping it stops them (docker compose stop); the startup checklist says whether Docker is running. The ports are Docker's: a compose app has none of its own.

key.description: Short name, unique in the profile.

type.description: The app type: what lazyrunner does with the app follows from it.

file.description: Optional. The compose file, from cwd; without it Docker's own (compose.yaml, docker-compose.yml, with its override file).

cwd.description: Optional. The folder of the compose file, from the repo root (the root without it).

services.description: Optional. The services it runs; all of the file's without it.

env.description: Optional. Environment variables docker compose gets on top of lazyrunner's own: the compose file's ${VARIABLES}.

dependsOn.description: Optional. The apps it calls, by key: the stack map (K) draws these edges dashed.

preset.title: A preset ("presets")
preset.description: What a language needs to run as a command app ("preset" names it): each field the app leaves out comes from the first of the preset's options that holds in the app's folder and has it, else from the preset (env merged, the app's own on top). lazyrunner's own are in projects/presets (python, go, rust); a presets folder beside your profiles and a profile's "presets" add to them or replace them.

id.description: Its name, as "preset" says it (a profile's own presets go by their key).

detect.description: Optional. The files that mark a folder as this language's: profile check suggests the preset for a command app there, and profile init adds one.

tools.description: Optional. Programs the startup checklist shows with their versions.

path.description: Optional. Folders from the app's cwd put first on PATH when they exist, and where its programs are looked for first.

env.description: Optional. Variables for the app, under its own; {cwd} is its folder, {port} its port.

setup.description: Optional. What makes its path folder before its first install.

installFrom.description: Optional. The files its install installs from.

ready.description: Optional. When it counts as up, as a command app's ready.

line.description: Up once a line of its output matches this regular expression.

orPort.description: With line: or once its port listens.

http.description: Up once this path on its port answers with a 2xx.

errors.description: Optional. Regular expressions of an error line.

warnings.description: Optional. Regular expressions of a warning line.

frames.description: Optional. A regular expression of a stack frame, with file and line groups.

options.description: Optional. What depends on the folder: each option's fields apply when its when holds - one of its anyFile in the app's folder, its program on PATH - the first option with a field winning over the later ones and the preset's own.

anyFileContains.description: Holds when one of these files, from the app's folder, has its text (a plugin, a dependency).

task.title: A task ("tasks")
task.description: A one-off command run from the palette (: then its name) or by an agent (run_task) - seed the database, regenerate a client - in the background, beside the apps. Its output goes to the panel's log between a rule with its name and its result: how long it took against its usual time, and its first error line when it failed.

key.description: Short name, unique among the tasks.

run.description: The command, as a command app's run.

cwd.description: Optional. Where it runs, from the repo root (the root without it).

env.description: Optional. Variables it gets on top of lazyrunner's own; {cwd} is its folder.

serveVariant.title: A dev-server variant
serveVariant.description: The script starts a server on a port (vite, ng serve, next dev …). The app is up once the port listens.

label.description: Shown in the column next to the script.

port.description: The dev server's port, unless the script itself says --port <n>.

buildVariant.title: A watch-build variant
buildVariant.description: The script builds and keeps watching, and a .NET app serves the output. The app is up once ready.file is written.

label.description: Shown in the column next to the script.

servedBy.description: The key of the .NET app that serves the build: w opens the app on its port.

file.description: A file the build writes, relative to dir: the app is ready once it is newer than the start.

when.description: When the variant applies; without it, always.

packageScript.description: The variant applies on a checkout whose package.json has this script (so it can differ per branch).
